title: Deriv
description: A symbolic differentiator in LISP. Give it an expression and a variable, and it prints the derivative.
versionOrder: Disk saves have no recorded order or dates beyond their source comments. Any ordering here is a presentation guess.

attribution.text: I wrote this in LISP. It runs on LISP 3.72, © 1981 Ronald L. Nicol, distributed by SuperSoft. Preserved here for small-scale archival use.

howTo: At the > prompt, type an infix expression in parentheses and press Enter, then type the variable and press Enter. For example, (X * X) and then X. Use [ for a power, :+: for plus, :-: for minus, * and /, and functions such as (SIN X).
Files cannot be saved: the disk is write-protected in this player. BREAK returns to the LISP prompt.
quickHelp: Type (X * X), Enter, then X, Enter. [ is a power; :+: and :-: add and subtract.
